confirmed_findings: Disabling mosaic (mosaic=0.0 vs 1.0) and reducing scale jitter (scale=0.15 vs 0.5) caused model-wide degradation, proven by sharp drops in road sign (-25.00 pp) and manhole (-10.12 pp) despite 100% identical training and test data.
The M1.8 and M1.11 waterlogging test splits share 0 overlapping images (0% overlap); therefore, the benchmark comparison was not a controlled paired experiment.
best.pt corresponds to Epoch 56 (peak fitness 0.39188), while Epoch 76 represents the early stopping termination epoch (last.pt).
Late-stage overfitting occurred between Epoch 56 and 76, where training box loss dropped from 0.7622 to 0.6273 while validation loss rose slightly from 1.4845 to 1.4947.
suggested_findings: Consolidating fragmented boxes reduced waterlogging training instances from 315 to 124 (60.6% drop), starving the feature extractor of critical bounding box gradients.

Introducing 19 negative waterlogging training images (24.4% of waterlogging data) caused excessive prediction suppression, leading to an 88% False Negative rate on held-out test puddles with model confidences depressed to 0.05-0.18.
inconclusive_findings: The isolated effect of canonical orientation vs 90/270 degree rotation cannot be isolated without a dedicated single-variable ablation experiment.
recommended_next_step: Module 1.13: Restore standard YOLO augmentations (mosaic=1.0, scale=0.5) with gravity constraints preserved (degrees=0.0, flipud=0.0), recalibrate negative sample ratio to ~10%, and perform a controlled paired evaluation on both M1.8 and M1.11 test splits.
